priority_rationale: Putrebactin synthase PubC (Q0HWI9) is a reviewed, protein-level NIS synthetase with experimentally cited native activity (PubMed 18630910). It catalyzes ATP-dependent head-to-tail dimerization of N-hydroxy-N-succinylputrescine (HSP) to pre-putrebactin, then macrocyclization. Each HSP carries both reacting ends, a succinyl carboxylate and a 4-aminobutyl NH3+. The native amide bond is therefore an acyl-adenylate carboxylate from an end-capped C4 dicarboxylate half, attacked by a primary amine on an aminoalkyl chain. This is the closest local match to glutarate plus cadaverine, and the iterative head-to-tail chemistry also fits the polyamide goal. The acyl-adenylate assignment is high confidence. Gaps remain: no direct glutarate or cadaverine data, chain lengths one carbon longer in the targets, no hydroxamate, and inverted distal charges. | accommodation context=0.41
